q: Select all records from a table
a: SELECT * FROM employees;

q: Select specific columns from a table
a: SELECT first_name, last_name, salary FROM employees;

q: Filter records using WHERE clause
a: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary > 50000;

q: Sort records in ascending order
a: SELECT * FROM employees ORDER BY salary ASC;

q: Sort records in descending order
a: SELECT * FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC;

q: Count total number of records in a table
a: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM employees;

q: Find the maximum salary
a: SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees;

q: Find the minimum salary
a: SELECT MIN(salary) FROM employees;

q: Calculate the average salary
a: SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees;

q: Find the sum of all salaries
a: SELECT SUM(salary) FROM employees;

q: Display the first 5 records in SQL
a: SELECT * FROM employees LIMIT 5;

q: Find distinct values in a column
a: SELECT DISTINCT department FROM employees;

q: Filter records with multiple conditions using AND
a: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary > 50000 AND department = 'IT';

q: Filter records with multiple conditions using OR
a: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE department = 'IT' OR department = 'HR';

q: Find records where a column value is NULL
a: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL;

q: Find records where a column value is NOT NULL
a: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NOT NULL;

q: Find records using the LIKE operator
a: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE first_name LIKE 'A%';

q: Find records using the IN operator
a: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE department IN ('IT', 'HR', 'Finance');

q: Find records within a range using BETWEEN
a: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary BETWEEN 40000 AND 80000;

q: Alias column names
a: SELECT first_name AS 'First Name', salary AS 'Annual Salary' FROM employees;

q: Concatenate two columns
a: SELECT CONCAT(first_name, ' ', last_name) AS full_name FROM employees;

q: Convert text to uppercase
a: SELECT UPPER(first_name) FROM employees;

q: Convert text to lowercase
a: SELECT LOWER(first_name) FROM employees;

q: Get the current date
a:
SELECT CURDATE(); -- MySQL
SELECT GETDATE(); -- SQL Server
SELECT CURRENT_DATE; -- PostgreSQL

q: Get the length of a string
a:
SELECT LENGTH(first_name) FROM employees; -- MySQL
SELECT LEN(first_name) FROM employees; -- SQL Server

q: Round a number to 2 decimal places
a: SELECT ROUND(salary, 2) FROM employees;

q: Find employees with salary greater than 50000
a: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary > 50000;

q: Find the first name starting with 'A'
a: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE first_name LIKE 'A%';

q: Sort by multiple columns
a: SELECT * FROM employees ORDER BY department ASC, salary DESC;

q: Use NOT operator
a: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE NOT department = 'IT';

q: Find the number of employees in each department
a: SELECT department, COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM employees GROUP BY department;

q: Get the highest salary in each department
a: SELECT department, MAX(salary) AS max_salary FROM employees GROUP BY department;

q: Find departments with more than 5 employees
a: SELECT department, COUNT(*) AS emp_count FROM employees GROUP BY department HAVING COUNT(*) > 5;

q: Find duplicate emails in the Employee table
a: SELECT email, COUNT(*) FROM employees GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

q: Display duplicate records with their count
a: SELECT email, COUNT(*) AS duplicate_count FROM employees GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

q: Delete duplicate records from a table
a: DELETE FROM employees WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT MIN(id) FROM employees GROUP BY email);

q: Find employees without managers
a: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL;

q: Find employees joined in the last 3 months
a: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE join_date >= DATE_SUB(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 3 MONTH);

q: Fetch the last 3 records in SQL
a: SELECT * FROM employees ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 3;

q: Fetch alternate rows (odd rows) from a table
a: SELECT * FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY id) AS row_num FROM employees) AS temp WHERE row_num % 2 = 1;

q: Fetch even rows from a table
a: SELECT * FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY id) AS row_num FROM employees) AS temp WHERE row_num % 2 = 0;

q: Find the second highest salary
a: SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees);

q: Find the Nth highest salary
a: SELECT DISTINCT salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET N-1;

q: Find the highest salary without using MAX()
a: SELECT salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 1;

q: Swap two column values
Perform INNER JOIN between two tables
a: SELECT e.first_name, d.department_name FROM employees e INNER JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id;

q: Perform LEFT JOIN
a: SELECT e.first_name, d.department_name FROM employees e LEFT JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id;

q: Perform RIGHT JOIN
a: SELECT e.first_name, d.department_name FROM employees e RIGHT JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id;

q: Perform FULL OUTER JOIN
a: SELECT e.first_name, d.department_name FROM employees e FULL OUTER JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id;

q: Perform SELF JOIN
a: SELECT e1.first_name AS employee, e2.first_name AS manager FROM employees e1 LEFT JOIN employees e2 ON e1.manager_id = e2.id;

q: Fetch common records from two tables without JOIN
a: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE department_id IN (SELECT id FROM departments);

q: Use UNION to combine results
a: SELECT first_name FROM employees WHERE department = 'IT' UNION SELECT first_name FROM employees WHERE department = 'HR';

q: Use UNION ALL
a: SELECT first_name FROM employees WHERE department = 'IT' UNION ALL SELECT first_name FROM employees WHERE department = 'HR';

q: Find employees whose salary is above average
a: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees);

q: Find the department with the highest employee count
a: SELECT department, COUNT(*) AS emp_count FROM employees GROUP BY department ORDER BY emp_count DESC LIMIT 1;

q: Create a copy of a table
a: CREATE TABLE employees_backup AS SELECT * FROM employees;

q: Copy only structure (not data)
a: CREATE TABLE employees_structure LIKE employees;

q: Insert data from one table to another
a: INSERT INTO employees_backup SELECT * FROM employees;

q: Update records based on a condition
a: UPDATE employees SET salary = salary * 1.10 WHERE department = 'IT';

q: Delete records based on a condition
a: DELETE FROM employees WHERE join_date < '2020-01-01';

q: Find employees with names containing 'an'
a: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE first_name LIKE '%an%';

q: Find employees whose names start with A and end with N
a: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE first_name LIKE 'A%N';

q: Use CASE statement for conditional logic
a: SELECT first_name, salary, CASE WHEN salary > 70000 THEN 'High' WHEN salary > 40000 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Low' END AS salary_grade FROM employees;

q: Find employees hired in a specific year
a: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE YEAR(join_date) = 2023;

q: Calculate age from date of birth
a: SELECT first_name, TIMESTAMPDIFF(YEAR, date_of_birth, CURDATE()) AS age FROM employees;

q: Get the day, month, and year from a date
a: SELECT DAY(join_date) AS day, MONTH(join_date) AS month, YEAR(join_date) AS year FROM employees;

q: Find records from the last 7 days
a: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE join_date >= DATE_SUB(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 7 DAY);

q: Add a new column to a table
a: ALTER TABLE employees ADD COLUMN phone VARCHAR(15);

q: Drop a column from a table
a: ALTER TABLE employees DROP COLUMN phone;

q: Rename a column
a: ALTER TABLE employees RENAME COLUMN old_name TO new_name;

q: Use ROW_NUMBER() to rank employees by salary
a: SELECT first_name, salary, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rank FROM employees;

q: Use RANK() function
a: SELECT first_name, salary, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rank FROM employees;

q: Use DENSE_RANK() function
a: SELECT first_name, salary, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS dense_rank FROM employees;

q: Find the top 3 salaries in each department
a: SELECT * FROM (SELECT first_name, department, salary, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rank FROM employees) AS ranked WHERE rank <= 3;

q: Use PARTITION BY in window functions
a: SELECT first_name, department, salary, AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department) AS dept_avg_salary FROM employees;

q: Calculate running total of salaries
a: SELECT first_name, salary, SUM(salary) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS running_total FROM employees;

q: Find the difference between current and previous row
a: SELECT first_name, salary, salary - LAG(salary) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS salary_diff FROM employees;

q: Use LEAD() to get the next row value
a: SELECT first_name, salary, LEAD(salary) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS next_salary FROM employees;

q: Find employees earning more than their manager
a: SELECT e.first_name, e.salary FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.id WHERE e.salary > m.salary;

q: Find employees with the same salary
a: SELECT e1.first_name, e1.salary FROM employees e1 JOIN employees e2 ON e1.salary = e2.salary AND e1.id != e2.id;

q: Use CTE (Common Table Expression)
a: WITH high_earners AS (SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary > 70000) SELECT * FROM high_earners;

q: Use recursive CTE to show employee hierarchy
a: WITH RECURSIVE emp_hierarchy AS (SELECT id, first_name, manager_id, 1 AS level FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT e.id, e.first_name, e.manager_id, eh.level + 1 FROM employees e JOIN emp_hierarchy eh ON e.manager_id = eh.id) SELECT * FROM emp_hierarchy;

q: Pivot data (rows to columns)
a: SELECT first_name, MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2021 THEN salary END) AS '2021', MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2022 THEN salary END) AS '2022', MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2023 THEN salary END) AS '2023' FROM employee_salaries GROUP BY first_name;

q: Unpivot data (columns to rows)
a: SELECT first_name, 'Jan' AS month, jan_sales AS sales FROM sales UNION ALL SELECT first_name, 'Feb', feb_sales FROM sales UNION ALL SELECT first_name, 'Mar', mar_sales FROM sales;

q: Find employees with salary greater than all in HR department
a: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary > ALL (SELECT salary FROM employees WHERE department = 'HR');

q: Find employees with salary greater than any in HR department
a: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary > ANY (SELECT salary FROM employees WHERE department = 'HR');

q: Use EXISTS clause
a: SELECT * FROM employees e WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM departments d WHERE d.id = e.department_id);

q: Find departments with no employees
a: SELECT d.* FROM departments d WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM employees e WHERE e.department_id = d.id);

q: Find the median salary
a: SELECT AVG(salary) AS median FROM (SELECT salary, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY salary) AS row_num, COUNT(*) OVER () AS total_count FROM employees) AS temp WHERE row_num IN (FLOOR((total_count + 1) / 2), CEIL((total_count + 1) / 2));

q: Find the mode (most frequent value)
a: SELECT salary FROM employees GROUP BY salary ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1;

q: Calculate cumulative percentage
a: SELECT first_name, salary, SUM(salary) OVER (ORDER BY salary) * 100.0 / SUM(salary) OVER () AS cumulative_percentage FROM employees;

q: Find gaps in sequential numbers
a: SELECT id + 1 AS missing_id FROM employees e WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM employees WHERE id = e.id + 1) AND id < (SELECT MAX(id) FROM employees);

q: Create a dense sequence of numbers
a: WITH RECURSIVE numbers AS (SELECT 1 AS n UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM numbers WHERE n < 100) SELECT n FROM numbers;

q: Find consecutive login dates
a: WITH login_groups AS (SELECT user_id, login_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY login_date) AS rn, DATE_SUB(login_date, INTERVAL ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY login_date) DAY) AS grp FROM user_logins) SELECT user_id, MIN(login_date) AS start_date, MAX(login_date) AS end_date, COUNT(*) AS consecutive_days FROM login_groups GROUP BY user_id, grp HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3;

q: Calculate moving average
a: SELECT first_name, salary, AVG(salary) OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS moving_avg FROM employees;

q: Find year-over-year growth
a: SELECT year, revenue, LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY year) AS prev_year_revenue, (revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY year)) * 100.0 / LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY year) AS yoy_growth FROM company_revenue;

q: Implement full-text search
a: SELECT * FROM articles WHERE MATCH(title, content) AGAINST('database optimization' IN NATURAL LANGUAGE MODE);

q: Find the longest streak of consecutive events
a: WITH streaks AS (SELECT event_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY event_date) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY event_date) AS streak_group FROM user_events) SELECT COUNT(*) AS longest_streak FROM streaks GROUP BY user_id, streak_group ORDER BY longest_streak DESC LIMIT 1;

q: Implement pagination efficiently
a: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE id > (SELECT id FROM employees ORDER BY id LIMIT 20 OFFSET 0) ORDER BY id LIMIT 20;

q: Find overlapping date ranges
a: SELECT e1.first_name, e2.first_name FROM employee_projects e1 JOIN employee_projects e2 ON e1.project_id = e2.project_id AND e1.id < e2.id WHERE e1.start_date <= e2.end_date AND e1.end_date >= e2.start_date;

q: Find the top performing employee in each department
a: SELECT * FROM (SELECT first_name, department, sales, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY sales DESC) AS rank FROM employees) AS ranked WHERE rank = 1;

q: Calculate retention rate
a: SELECT ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN month_diff = 1 THEN user_id END) * 100.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT user_id), 2) AS retention_rate FROM (SELECT user_id, DATEDIFF(MONTH, LAG(login_date) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY login_date), login_date) AS month_diff FROM user_logins) AS temp;

q: Transpose rows into comma-separated values
a: SELECT department, GROUP_CONCAT(first_name ORDER BY first_name SEPARATOR ', ') AS employees FROM employees GROUP BY department;

q: Find customers who purchased both Product A and Product B
a: SELECT customer_id FROM purchases WHERE product_name = 'Product A' INTERSECT SELECT customer_id FROM purchases WHERE product_name = 'Product B';

q: Calculate percentile rank
a: SELECT first_name, salary, PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary) AS percentile_rank FROM employees;

q: Find the first and last record in each group
a: SELECT department, FIRST_VALUE(first_name) OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY join_date) AS first_employee, LAST_VALUE(first_name) OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY join_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS last_employee FROM employees;

q: Implement a cross join
a: SELECT e.first_name, d.department_name FROM employees e CROSS JOIN departments d;

q: Find employees with maximum experience in each department
a: SELECT * FROM (SELECT *, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY DATEDIFF(CURDATE(), join_date) DESC) AS rank FROM employees) AS ranked WHERE rank = 1;

q: Calculate the difference between max and min salary per department
a: SELECT department, MAX(salary) - MIN(salary) AS salary_range FROM employees GROUP BY department;

q: Find all employees who report to the same manager
a: SELECT e1.first_name, e1.manager_id FROM employees e1 WHERE e1.manager_id IN (SELECT manager_id FROM employees GROUP BY manager_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1);
